successors.note: The state was a federal state of the German Empire from 1871 and ended in November 1918 (see the dissolve event); the Weimar Republic took over its land (People's State of Hesse). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-53 D01, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire; same change as fx-46 R122 for Bavaria); the hierarchy.csv row grand-duchy-of-hesse -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.

keyframe_review.note: Too large: 20,167 km2 (91 cells; 55 in Hesse, 30 in North Rhine-Westphalia) against the infobox 'Area: 9,300 km2 (1806)', a ratio of 2.17, beyond a factor of two. The 1807 shape (40 cells, 8,484 km2) is the same land without about 52 cells in Hesse; the page says 'Electoral Hesse lands were taken in 1806' and Cliopatria has no Electorate of Hesse shape for 1806-1813, so the extra cells are probably Hesse-Kassel land occupied in 1806. The correction is the 1807 shape.

correction.text: Hesse-Darmstadt of 1806: Starkenburg, Upper Hesse and the Duchy of Westphalia, 9,300 km2 in the infobox; the shape is the 1807 Cliopatria shape without the extra 1806 cells

keyframe_review.note: 8,484 km2 against the infobox 9,300 km2 (1806): ratio 0.91. The shape holds Starkenburg, Upper Hesse and the Duchy of Westphalia (20 cells in North Rhine-Westphalia). The 1809 Kloppenheim and Schiffenberg merger and the 1810 Babenhausen exchange are too small to show.
8,615 km2, the same land with the 1809 Teutonic Order lands (Kloppenheim, Schiffenberg Abbey) merged on 24 April 1809 and the 1810 exchanges; ratio 0.93 to the infobox 9,300 km2.
8,460 km2, unchanged in extent; no territorial change in 1811-1814 on the page.
8,372 km2, unchanged; the Duchy of Westphalia is still Hessian in 1814 (the Congress of Vienna met 1814-15).

Cliopatria holds the 1814 land through 1819. The Westphalia page: 'In 1815 the Congress of Vienna awarded the Duchy of Westphalia to Prussia in exchange for important lands west of the Rhine' and incorporated it into Prussia's Province of Westphalia 'the same year'; Hesse-Homburg's independence was recognised in 1815 (Hesse-Homburg page). So the 1815 shape loses Westphalia and Homburg; the left-bank Rhine district followed in 1816 (see grand-duchy-of-hesse_1816). Applies to 1815 only.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1815 shape without the Duchy of Westphalia and Hesse-Homburg; for 1815 only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1816-1819, which Cliopatria draws with the pre-Vienna shape. The Rhenish Hesse page: Louis I 'received the district on the left bank of the Rhine' in compensation for his Westphalian lands and the region 'was part of the Grand Duchy of Hesse ... from 1816'; the Hesse page: the grand duchy 'received part of the Mont-Tonnerre department, including Mainz'; population about 630,000 in 1816. The shape is Cliopatria's 1820 shape (10,617 km2 against the infobox 8,345 km2 for 1815, ratio 1.27).

correction.text: the grand duchy after the exchange: Starkenburg, Upper Hesse and Rhenish Hesse, without Westphalia

keyframe_review.note: 10,617 km2 against the infobox 8,345 km2 (1815) and 7,682 km2 (1866): ratios 1.27 and 1.38, within a factor of two (the cells over-fill the Rhine valley). Starkenburg, Upper Hesse and Rhenish Hesse; the page lists no territorial change between 1816 and 1866.
Same 44 cells as 1820; the page's 1848-1849 events (serfdom abolished 8 March 1848, eleven government districts 31 July 1848, the 1849 electoral law) are constitutional, not territorial.
Same land as 1820 through 1865; no change on the page.

New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Hesse shape for 1866-1867. The treaty of 3 September 1866: Hesse 'lost 82 km2' (as the page gives it), Hesse-Homburg 'passed to Prussia', 'The Biedenkopf district and the Hessian Hinterland were annexed' and 'Amt Dorheim was given to the grand duchy'. The shape is Cliopatria's 1868 shape; before September 1866 the 1853 shape holds. The page's 82 km2 is far below the 7 cells (about 1,800 km2) by which the 1868 shape is smaller than the 1853 one; the Hinterland and Biedenkopf alone are larger.

correction.text: Hesse after the Prussian annexations of September 1866: without Biedenkopf and the Hinterland

keyframe_review.note: 8,786 km2 against the infobox 7,682 km2 (1866), ratio 1.14. Oberhessen (3,287 km2, the NGC table's 'Hesse' row) was a member of the North German Confederation from 1867, the south stayed outside until November 1870 ('the Grand Duchy of Hesse remained outside ... although Oberhessen ... did join'): an association, not territory.

7,383 km2 (32 cells): seven fewer cells than 1868, exactly the six cells that Cliopatria's 1870 North German Confederation shape overlaps with the 1868 Hesse shape, plus one. The page records no Hessian cession in 1870 (Hesse joined the confederation on 20 October 1870, treaty of 15 November 1870, German Empire 18 January 1871) and its infobox area is 7,682 km2 in 1866 and 7,688 km2 in 1910, so the 1868 land stands.

correction.text: the 1868 land unchanged: joining the North German Confederation in 1870 is membership, not a cession

ledger.note: 13 August 1806: Louis I of Hesse-Darmstadt becomes Grand Duke. The page: 'Louis I announced the promotion to grand duchy and the territories received under the Confederation of the Rhine treaty' by an edict of 13 August 1806 (infobox 'Established 13 August 1806'); the CoR treaty is dated 12 July 1806 in other pages. The core is the researcher's reading: the Cliopatria 1807 shape.

region.text: Starkenburg around Darmstadt, Upper Hesse around Giessen and the Duchy of Westphalia: Hesse-Darmstadt as a grand duchy

ledger.note: 1806: Hesse-Homburg is mediatised into the new grand duchy. Frederick V 'lost his lands in the German mediatisation of 1806' when Hesse-Homburg 'was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Hesse'; it was part of Hesse-Darmstadt 'from 1806 to 1815'. The page gives the year only; August is placed with the elevation to a grand duchy.

region.text: Homburg vor der Höhe, the Landgraviate of Hesse-Homburg (221 km2 after 1815)

ledger.note: 24 April 1809: the Teutonic Order lands are merged. 'Napoleon ordered the abolition of the Teutonic Order, merging Kloppenheim and Schiffenberg Abbey into the grand duchy.' Too small to show on the map; the circle round Giessen stands for Schiffenberg, Kloppenheim is not located.

region.text: Schiffenberg Abbey near Giessen and Kloppenheim, the Teutonic Order lands merged into the grand duchy

ledger.note: 1810: Babenhausen goes to Starkenburg. A treaty with France, dated 11 May 1810 and signed 17 October 1810, 'granted areas taken from Electoral Hesse in 1806'; 'Babenhausen went to Starkenburg'. The page also names a three-way agreement with France and Baden of August 1810 and a treaty of 11 November 1810 exchanging territory, with no place named. The month is the signing; the giver is France as the treaty party.
1815: the Congress of Vienna frees Hesse-Homburg. 'But in 1815, the Congress of Vienna forced Hesse-Darmstadt to recognize the independence of Hesse-Homburg.'

region.text: Homburg vor der Höhe, the Landgraviate of Hesse-Homburg (221 km2 after 1815)

ledger.note: 1815: the Duchy of Westphalia goes to Prussia. 'In 1815 the Congress of Vienna awarded the Duchy of Westphalia to Prussia in exchange for important lands west of the Rhine' and it was incorporated into the Province of Westphalia 'the same year'. The Hesse page: Hesse received part of Mont-Tonnerre, including Mainz, 'in exchange for the Duchy of Westphalia, which went to Prussia'; a treaty of 30 June 1816 with Austria and Prussia regulated the region.

region.text: the Duchy of Westphalia, the Sauerland around Arnsberg, the part of the 1807 shape in North Rhine-Westphalia

ledger.note: 1816: the state takes the name 'Grand Duchy of Hesse and by Rhine'. Population about 630,000.

1816: Rhenish Hesse joins the grand duchy. Louis I 'received the district on the left bank of the Rhine' in compensation; the region 'was part of the Grand Duchy of Hesse ... from 1816'. The Hesse page names Mainz and the Mont-Tonnerre department and a treaty of 30 June 1816 with Austria and Prussia (patents of 8 July 1816). The giver is the former French department under allied administration; the Austrian and Bavarian share (Worms and Pfeddersheim) is in the Bavaria and Austria dossiers.

region.text: Rhenish Hesse, the 'district on the left bank of the Rhine' with Mainz and Worms, the part of the 1820 shape in Rhineland-Palatinate

ledger.note: 24 March 1866: Hesse-Homburg returns to Hesse-Darmstadt. 'With the death of Landgrave Ferdinand on 24 March 1866, the Hesse-Homburg dynasty's male line came to an end'; 'Hesse-Homburg returned to the Grand Duke of Hesse, while Meisenheim fell to Prussia.'

region.text: Homburg vor der Höhe, the Landgraviate of Hesse-Homburg (221 km2 after 1815)

ledger.note: 3 September 1866: Hesse loses Biedenkopf, the Hinterland and Hesse-Homburg to Prussia. 'The Biedenkopf district and the Hessian Hinterland were annexed'; Hesse-Homburg, inherited in 1866, 'passed to Prussia' (the Hesse-Homburg page: 'forced to cede the territory to Prussia in September of the same year'); Prussian troops had occupied Darmstadt on 31 July 1866. The page's own loss figure of 82 km2 is inconsistent with the annexed districts.

ledger.note: 3 September 1866: Amt Dorheim is given to the grand duchy. The page says 'Amt Dorheim was given to the grand duchy'; the region is the 1868-only cells of the Cliopatria shape, the giver (Prussia, with Hesse-Homburg's lands) is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 9 November 1918: the grand duke is removed. Infobox 'German Revolution: 9 November 1918'; Ernest Louis was 'removed from power on 9 November 1918' and 'he never issued an explicit abdication'; 'the grand duchy was overthrown and replaced by the People's State of Hesse'; infobox status 'Federal State of the German Empire (1871-1918)'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War

zones.text: the Biedenkopf district and the Hessian Hinterland, the cells of the 1853 shape missing in 1868

wars.outcome: Hesse, on Austria's side, lost the Battle of Frohnhofen near Aschaffenburg (13 July 1866) and the Battle of Tauberbischofsheim (24 July); Prussian troops occupied Darmstadt on 31 July. The treaty of 3 September 1866 cost Hesse the Biedenkopf district, the Hinterland and Hesse-Homburg and Upper Hesse joined the North German Confederation.
wars.note: The battles were fought outside Hesse (Bavaria and Baden); the only fighting zone inside Hesse is the Prussian occupation, which has no page date for its end. The ceded land is the zone.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Hesse joined the North German Confederation on 20 October 1870 during the war; no territory changed.
wars.note: Listed so that the reviewer can see it was considered; the war did not move Hesse's border.

certainty.note: The Napoleonic grand duchy was assembled from the Final Recess lands of 1803 and the 1806 mediatisations; the page names no boundaries and Westphalia was a detached exclave.

Boundaries from the treaty of 30 June 1816 (Rhenish Hesse) and from the treaty of 3 September 1866 (Biedenkopf, the Hinterland, Hesse-Homburg). 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes: Cliopatria shapes: 1806 is about 2.2 times the infobox area (adjust to the 1807 shape); 1807-1814 ok; 1815-1819 is the pre-Vienna shape (1815 loses Westphalia and Hesse-Homburg, the left-bank district follows in 1816: new keyframe grand-duchy-of-hesse_1816); 1866-1867 is a Cliopatria gap (new keyframe grand-duchy-of-hesse_1866); 1870 is adjusted to the 1868 land. The pages disagree on the year of the Westphalian transfer: the Westphalia and Hesse pages say 1815 (Congress of Vienna), the Hesse page's treaty of 30 June 1816 regulated the region and the Rhine district belongs to Hesse from 1816; the kingdom-of-prussia dossier dates the Westphalian gain 9 June 1815. Not settled within the five-page budget: which Hessian lands the 1806 shape adds ('Electoral Hesse lands were taken in 1806', 'The Electorate of Cologne was gained'), the August-November 1810 exchange with Baden and France (no place named), the 1806 mediatisations of the Standesherren (Isenburg, Solms, Erbach and others, not named on the page), the 82 km2 loss figure of 1866 against the annexed districts, and whether Hesse gave Worms and Pfeddersheim to Bavaria in 1816-1819 (the kingdom-of-bavaria dossier records a gain from Hesse). 1867-1870: Oberhessen was a member of the North German Confederation while the grand duchy stayed outside: an association, drawn as no territory change. Dossier ends in January 1871 as the sibling German states do, although the grand duchy lasted until 9 November 1918. Counterparts without a dossier: Landgraviate of Hesse-Homburg (to 1866, 221 km2), Teutonic Order lands, Mont-Tonnerre department. Coordinates used for places the gazetteer lacks: Homburg (8.62E, 50.23N) and Babenhausen (8.96E, 49.96N). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (grand-duchy-of-hesse_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row grand-duchy-of-hesse -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. Ernest Louis never issued an explicit abdication; he was removed from power on 9 November 1918.
